newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon downgrades IBM.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Salomon downgrades IBM.

text.p: -- Salomon Brothers computer systems analyst John Jones said he downgraded International Business Machines Corp to buy from strong buy and lowered his earnings estimates for both 1997 and 1998.
-- In a published note, Jones said he cut his 1997 estimate to $12.90 per share from $13.20, and reduced his 1998 estimate to $15 from $15.25.
-- He forecast a long-term price target of $180-$185 per share. In December he set a target of $185.
-- Jones noted that IBM stock has gained 52 percent since he issued a strong buy rating on August 27, 1996.
-- The analyst said IBM's 1996 fourth quarter earnings of $3.93 per share were increased by $0.30 a share by a lower-than-expected tax rate of 29.9 percent.
-- IBM had guided analysts to expect a 35 percent tax rate for the fourth quarter, analysts said.

-- Jones said IBM's fourth quarter charge of roughly $200 million for restructuring European operations was about $100 million less than expected, which helped boost fourth quarter earnings by $0.20 per share.
-- He said his lower estimates for 1997 and 1998 reflect slightly lower assumptions about gross profit margins and tax rates.
-- He said he reduced his 1997 revenue forecast by $1.49 billon, to $81.3 billion.

-- Jones said $1 billion of the reduction was tied to a change in his view of how much currency translation will reduce recorded revenues, and $490 million reflected lower mainframe, workstation and storage revenues.
-- "IBM appears to be managing results for the longer term," Jones wrote, noting that IBM's investments in manufacturing are yielding the tax rate advantages that are boosting its bottom line.
-- "Such actions underscore our long-term support for the stock," he said.
